subject: Ingest pipeline classification & cross-border provenance questions
messages:
From: Jake Turner <jake.turner@medisync.health>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: privacy+ops@medisync.health
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Ingest pipeline classification & provenance questions

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks again for the demo last week. The security team at Medisync asked me to follow up with a few detailed questions so we can close the privacy assessment and move to contract review. High level: we need to verify how PII is classified at ingest, which subprocessors touch raw inputs, and what evidence you can provide that provenance is maintained (esp. for cross-border routing).

Specific asks:
1) At the point a customer request hits Redwood (hosted API or Dedicated gateway), what fields are classified as PII vs. non-PII? Is classification automated or customer-provided?
2) Which subprocessors have access to raw token-level data during the inference flow (including batching/queueing, caching layers, and observability telemetry)?
3) How does the system tag/record provenance metadata (origin IP, region, model version, request id) so we can prove where data was processed and when? Are these artifacts exportable to us for audits?
4) For cross-border fallbacks (e.g., routing to eu-variant), what controls prevent residency leakage?

If you can reply with short answers + artifacts we can share with our compliance team that would be ideal. Appreciate a response by end of week — Medisync is targeting contract signature in early August.

Best,
Jake
Jake Turner
Privacy Program Manager | Medisync Health

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Turner <jake.turner@medisync.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Jul 2028 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ingest pipeline classification & provenance questions

Jake —

Thanks for the clear list. I pulled in Marissa (privacy ops) and Karthik (inference infra) so we can provide concrete artifacts. High-level answers first, then I’ll attach a short set of evidence pointers.

1) Classification at ingest:
- Redwood does not perform PII extraction automatically by default. We store raw request payloads by default in transient buffers for inference. Classification is done via two mechanisms: customer-supplied classification metadata (recommended) and an optional Redwood-managed PII-scanner plugin that can be enabled per-tenant.
- We consider the following as PII by default when the scanner is enabled: direct identifiers (names, SSNs, email addresses), contact info, and medical identifiers (MRNs) if detected by pattern match. Free-text that requires NLP classification is flagged but left to customer confirmation.

2) Subprocessors with token-level access:
- Minimal set: Redwood inference runtime (hosted), object storage provider for temporary caching, and our telemetry pipeline (aggregator). For Dedicated customers who choose isolated pools, subprocessors are reduced to the infra provider and optional telemetry vendor (if enabled).
- We maintain an up-to-date subprocessor roster; I’m attaching the roster CSV and the subprocessor classification matrix (access scoping column included).

3) Provenance metadata and evidence export:
- Each request is stamped with a stable request_id and an immutable provenance bundle that includes: request_id, model_version, node_region, ingress_ip (redacted on request), timestamp(s) for each pipeline stage, and processing tier (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Provenance bundles are stored for 90 days by default (configurable under Enterprise plans). Export: we can provide a signed provenance export (JSONL) for audit windows and integrate exports into your SIEM via push endpoints. I’ve linked the design doc and attached a snapshot diagram of the ingest flow.

4) Cross-border fallbacks and residency controls:
- Routing is policy-driven. Customers can set strict residency rules: (a) strict: never route out of primary region; (b) soft-fallback: prefer primary region, allow fallback to approved bucket of regions; (c) cost-fallback: allow cheapest region when primary exhausted.
- For strict residency, we enforce tenancy-level routing at the gateway and at the datastore layer; any fallback that would cross a geofence is blocked. For soft-fallback we log the event in the provenance bundle and redact PII according to customer policy prior to routing.

Artifacts attached / links below:
- ingest_dataflow_v2.png (annotated flow showing where provenance metadata is generated)
- subprocessor_roster_2028-07.csv (access scoping column)
- kms_attestation_2028-06.pdf (summary of KMS key custodianship and rotation)
- Design doc link: https://drive.redwood.ai/teams/privacy/medisync-ingest-diagram-v2

We can also run a short export exercise for Medisync on a demo tenant to show a provenance export and redaction pipeline. Happy to schedule a 30-minute session with Karthik.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Director, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Ingest pipeline classification & provenance questions

Jake —

Quick answers from infra: 
- Provenance export latency: for ~5M requests (30 day window) our bulk export pipeline typically produces a compressed JSONL export in ~45-90 minutes using on-cluster aggregation and parallel writers. If you need sub-30 minute turnarounds we can provision a higher parallelism job under an SLA (costed).
- Caching and object storage: by default transient KV caches (used for small prefix caching and batching) are regional and pinned to the serving region. We do not replicate transient caches across regions.
- For object storage used for batching spillover and temporary artifacts we use an S3-compatible gateway that is configured per-tenant; for Hosted customers we maintain regional buckets and do not multi-region-replicate without a tenant opt-in. Keys are never replicated across regions by default; replication requires explicit tenant configuration.

If you want a short runbook describing the export process and cost profile I can attach it.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

1) Can you confirm the retention window is configurable to 365 days under an Enterprise plan (we will need at least 1 year of provenance retention for audit purposes)?
2) Please include language in the DPA that lists which subprocessors may have transient access to raw request payloads and the controls (e.g., encryption at rest, role-based access, audited access) that limit that access.

If you can draft a short DPA annex bullet list for those points we’ll fold it into our redline. Looking forward to the demo export next week.
